1. Forbidden Planet (1956) This is the greatest science-fiction movie ever made. The Citizen Kane of science fiction. Disagree at your own peril.
  2. Blade Runner (1982) Hard to overestimate its influence. Along with Neuromancer, defines an entire genre of science-fiction.
  3. Aliens (1986) Again, hard to overestimate its influence. Still the best action-adventure movie ever made.
  4. 2001: A Space Odyssey (1968) Because it has to be on the list somewhere. It's the law.
  5. Akira (1988) Still so beautiful and thought-provoking. It's not axiomatic that there will be better some day.
  6. Things to Come (1936) If you call yourself a fan of science-fiction, it's pretty much mandatory that you track this down.

Plus both Things, the Universal Monster Movies, the first Godzilla, The Matrix, This Island Earth, The Terminator(s) I&II, Predator, The Day the Earth Stood Still, Serenity, etc, etc.

In terms of influence on the genre (and on world cinema in general) look no further than Akira Kurosawa's Seven Samurai (1954), Throne of Blood (1957), The Hidden Fortress (1958), Yojimbo (1961), and Sanjuro (1962). To borrow from Ebert:

Akira Kurosawa's "Seven Samurai" (1954) is not only a great film in its own right, but the source of a genre that would flow through the rest of the century. The critic Michael Jeck suggests that this was the first film in which a team is assembled to carry out a mission--an idea which gave birth to its direct Hollywood remake, "The Magnificent Seven," as well as "The Guns of Navarone," "The Dirty Dozen" and countless later war, heist and caper movies. Since Kurosawa's samurai adventure "Yojimbo" (1960) was remade as "A Fistful of Dollars" and essentially created the spaghetti Western, and since this movie and Kurosawa's "The Hidden Fortress" inspired George Lucas' "Star Wars" series, it could be argued that this greatest of filmmakers gave employment to action heroes for the next 50 years, just as a fallout from his primary purpose.
